conditions.note: HSV-2, on daily suppression since diagnosis

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

25 y/o woman starting a doctoral program in public health this fall; moved to Easthampton over the summer and wants a primary care home here. No complaints today.

PMH: genital HSV-2, diagnosed about three years ago by her previous PCP. Takes valacyclovir 500 mg every day for suppression and says it works; can't remember the last outbreak. Nothing else.
PSH: none.
Meds: valacyclovir 500 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
FHx: mother with hypothyroidism. Father with high blood pressure.
Social: never smoked, no alcohol, no drugs. Lives in an apartment in town. Single. Grad school full time with a research assistantship. Insurance through the university student plan.
Gyn: periods regular. Last Pap 2019 at her old office, she thinks normal. Thinks she had the HPV shots as a kid.

ROS: negative across the board.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Well-appearing. HEENT normal, neck without nodes or thyromegaly. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin clear. No genital exam today, no active lesions per patient.

A/P
1. Genital HSV-2, on suppression. Continue valacyclovir 500 mg daily. We'll take over refills once her current supply runs out.
2. Health maintenance. CBC, CMP, TSH (given mom's thyroid history), one-time HIV and hep C, urine chlamydia/GC. PHQ-2 is 0. Requesting old records for Pap and immunization history. Flu shot when it arrives in October.

Return for a physical next year, sooner as needed.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Delaney, your bloodwork from Tuesday is all normal: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, thyroid. HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative, and so were the urine chlamydia and gonorrhea tests. Nothing to do. Nice to have you with us.

documents.title: Prior Primary Care Records
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Records received by fax from prior primary care office, 41 pages, scanned to chart. Abstracted:
- 2018: clinic visit for painful genital sores; lesion swab PCR positive for HSV-2. Started valacyclovir, then switched to daily valacyclovir 500 mg for suppression; continued since.
- Pap July 2019: NILM.
- Immunizations: childhood series complete per state registry printout; Tdap 2007; HPV (quadrivalent) x3, 2008; COVID Pfizer 4/6/21 and 4/27/21 (card copy on file).
- No other diagnoses, no surgeries, NKDA.
Forwarded to PCP for review.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for flu vaccine. No fever today, no prior reactions to vaccines, not pregnant. Quadrivalent influenza 0.5 mL IM left deltoid, VIS given. Waited 15 minutes, no reaction.

documents.body: Pharmacy refill request for valacyclovir 500 mg, 1 tab daily. First fill from this office; prior prescriber was her old PCP. On med list, seen 8/24. Sent 90 days with 3 refills per PCP protocol.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL

Doing well. Second year of the program, teaching a section this fall. Valacyclovir daily, no breakthrough outbreaks this year. Sexually active with one male partner; condoms some of the time. Periods regular. Sleep okay.

Meds: valacyclovir 500 mg daily. NKDA.
Social: no tobacco, no alcohol.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Well. HEENT normal. Neck no nodes or thyroid enlargement. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Breasts deferred (age). Abdomen benign. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, no lesions; speculum exam normal cervix, Pap obtained. Skin clear. Mood bright, PHQ-2 1.

A/P
- Genital HSV-2: well controlled on suppression. Continue.
- Cervical screening: Pap today (last 2019).
- STI screen: urine CT/GC.
- Fasting lipid panel, first one.
- Flu and COVID bivalent next month when available.
RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Pap and Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your Pap came back normal, so the next one is due in three years. Cholesterol numbers look good, and the chlamydia and gonorrhea tests were negative. See you next fall, or sooner if anything comes up.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (quadrivalent) 0.5 mL IM right deltoid and Pfizer bivalent COVID booster 0.3 mL IM left deltoid. Screening negative, not pregnant. Tolerated both; observed 15 minutes. Expect a sore arm.
